question: What best describes disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: A medical research project carried out in tertiary hospitals
options.B: A clinical trial testing new pharmaceutical drug treatments
options.C: A one-time survey conducted during a disease outbreak
options.D: A continuous process of collecting and analyzing health data

explanation: Surveillance requires ongoing and systematic tracking rather than a single, isolated research event. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h1)

question: Why is disease surveillance considered a continuous loop rather than a one-time survey?

options.A: It reduces the financial burden on the federal ministry of health
options.B: It allows health workers to constantly monitor trends and act early
options.C: it eliminates the need for laboratory confirmation of illnesses
options.D: It ensures that patients visit the primary health centre every month

explanation: Continuous data flow helps public health teams spot anomalies and respond before infections spread widely. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h1)

question: The main goal of public health surveillance is to reduce what?

options.A: The total cost of running government teaching hospitals
options.B: Morbidity and mortality through timely public health action
options.C: The number of nursing students enrolled in training schools
options.D: The administrative duties assigned to primary health care coordinators

explanation: All surveillance activities ultimately aim to lower sickness and death rates in the community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h2)

question: A local government health team uses surveillance data to check if a recent polio immunization campaign worked. Which surveillance objective does this represent?
explanation: Assessing the success of an implemented vaccination drive falls under intervention evaluation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h2)

question: What characterizes passive surveillance in a health system?

options.A: Clinicians routinely submit reports to health authorities without prompting
options.B: Information is collected exclusively during emergency epidemic responses
options.C: Data is gathered from only one specialized teaching hospital
options.D: Health officers actively visit communities to search for sick patients

explanation: Passive surveillance relies on busy clinic staff remembering to send in their routine tally sheets. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h3)

question: When is active surveillance preferred over passive surveillance by health authorities?

options.A: When the ministry of health has zero funds for field operations
options.B: When routine clinic reports are completely free from any errors
options.C: During periods of long-term stability with no reported infections
options.D: During an active outbreak when every single case must be found

explanation: Active searching is labour-intensive and is deployed when high accuracy and urgent case finding are critical. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h3)

question: What is the very first step in the disease surveillance cycle?
explanation: Surveillance cannot begin without first gathering raw health facts from clinical and community sources. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h4)

question: Why is data dissemination considered a critical step in the surveillance process?

options.A: It replaces the need to analyze collected health records
options.B: It guarantees immediate international funding for local hospitals
options.C: It permanently stops patients from visiting traditional healers
options.D: It ensures stakeholders and decision-makers receive actionable intelligence

explanation: Information must reach the people who have the authority and resources to act on it. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h4)

question: Which of the following is a classic source of routine health surveillance data?
explanation: Legally mandated reporting of specific infectious conditions forms the backbone of data sources. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h5)

question: Why must surveillance systems include community sources alongside formal hospital records?

options.A: Many sick individuals never visit formal health facilities
options.B: Hospitals are legally prohibited from sharing patient data
options.C: Community informants are paid higher salaries than nurses
options.D: Laboratory tests are completely unnecessary in rural areas

explanation: Relying solely on hospitals misses people who self-medicate or visit traditional birth attendants. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h5)

question: What graphical tool is commonly used during an outbreak investigation to show the time course of an epidemic?
explanation: An epi curve plots cases by time of onset, helping investigators understand how the outbreak spread. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h6)

question: Why is establishing a clear case definition essential during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: It ensures everyone counts the exact same illness criteria
options.B: It automatically cures patients admitted to the isolation ward
options.C: It reduces the workload of environmental health officers
options.D: It eliminates the need for any laboratory blood tests

explanation: A standard definition prevents health workers from misclassifying unrelated ailments as part of the outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h6)

question: What is a primary surveillance duty of a nurse at a primary health centre?

options.B: Designing architectural layouts for isolation centres
options.C: Approving national public health financial budgets

explanation: Frontline nurses document and report infectious cases using standard tally books and forms. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h7)

question: How does a nurse's daily interaction with patients impact local disease surveillance?

options.A: It guarantees zero underreporting in rural health clinics
options.B: It enhances early detection of unusual illness patterns
options.C: It removes the need for community health extension workers
options.D: It completely stops the transmission of airborne infections

explanation: Nurses see patients first, making them uniquely positioned to spot clustering symptoms early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h7)

question: Which factor is a major cause of underreporting in disease surveillance systems?

options.A: Too many nurses working in rural health centers
options.B: Immediate internet access in every remote village
options.C: Heavy clinical workloads and lack of feedback
options.D: Excessive availability of rapid diagnostic test kits

explanation: Busy clinicians often view reporting paperwork as an added burden when they receive no feedback. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h8)

question: Why does a weak laboratory network severely damage a disease surveillance system?

options.A: Patients will completely stop visiting traditional healers
options.B: The government will stop funding all primary health clinics
options.C: Nurses will refuse to document patient names in registers
options.D: Suspected cases cannot be quickly and accurately confirmed

explanation: Without diagnostics, outbreaks rely on guesswork, delaying targeted public health interventions. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h8)
